A low volume of concentrated urine during dehydration is consistent with effective ADH signalling. A large volume of dilute urine despite concentrated blood may mean that too little ADH reaches the blood or that the kidney does not respond normally. One pattern alone cannot show which explanation is correct.Diabetes insipidus is a water-balance disorder involving too little effective ADH signalling.
